messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—even the kids in the streets know it now. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but how fast, and whether the ones holding the ropes will cut them first or be dragged down with them."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The leadership’s still locked in, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the banks hedging, the barracks whispering, the news changing its tune overnight. Nothing’s breaking yet, but if the wind shifts—even a little—this whole thing could tip either way. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual rules don’t apply anymore, and the people who’ve always known the score are suddenly acting like they’ve lost the script. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking like they’ve forgotten to be afraid, and the regime’s moves feel more like panic than control. But we still don’t know if this is real or a trap, so let’s stay sharp and keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different now—like the quiet before a storm. People aren’t just talking; they’re preparing, and even the ones who used to defend the regime are stepping back. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t just another crisis, and we may not have much time."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like people are holding their breath instead of shouting. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know which something."*"
Sender 7: "*"The cracks are showing—more than just the usual cracks. The inner circle’s quiet, the security forces are stepping back, and even the propaganda machine is stumbling over its own words. If you’ve got people you trust, now’s the time to talk to them—but keep it quiet, keep it careful. This isn’t a storm warning. It’s the storm."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—nothing loud yet, but the paint’s flaking in places you can see if you look close. My landlord, of all people, just asked if I had a backup plan, and the jokes in the café aren’t just jokes anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but not in the way they’d want us to notice. The cracks are showing, and not just in the usual places. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and not just for the usual reasons. The usual signs are all there, but quieter, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this could go fast, one way or the other."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the calm before a storm you can’t quite hear yet. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still holding, for now. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but the glue’s getting thinner—people are talking more, laughing darker, and the regime’s moving like it’s trying to outrun its own shadow. Not sure if it’s about to snap or just tightening its grip, but either way, we should all be ready to move fast if the wind changes."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another quiet stretch. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—businesses playing it safe, the courts stumbling over their own rules, and even the security forces acting like they’re saving their energy for something. No one’s running yet, but no one’s fully trusting the ground under their feet either. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s before a storm or a sigh of relief. The top’s still holding together, but the cracks are showing in the little things—money moving sideways, plans getting delayed, even the shopkeepers whispering what they’d never say out loud. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The regime’s still dangerous, but for the first time in a while, it feels like the ground might shift under us."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like fear, more like a held breath. Small things are slipping: paychecks arrive early, hospitals run dry, and the TV cuts out just long enough to make you wonder. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are starting to show in the places that matter. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the quiet before something, not necessarily the something itself."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are starting to sweat—small leaks, but the damp is spreading. Keep your circles tight, but don’t be surprised if the quiet ones start talking soon. And maybe stock up on basics, just in case the usual channels get clogged again."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s grip is loosening, but no one’s sure if it’s slipping or just shifting. The elites are hedging, the streets are getting bolder, and the courts are stalling, but the security forces are still waiting. Could be the calm before something, or just the quiet of a system holding its breath. Either way, we should be ready for either."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just the usual tremors. The guards are watching each other now, and even the quiet ones are packing their bags. Keep your heads down, but stay ready. The air feels different."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who never spoke before are asking questions now. The regime’s still putting on a show, but the script’s falling apart behind the scenes. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a sprint, it’s the first real breath we’ve had in years."*"
Sender 20: "*"The cracks are showing faster than they can patch—fuel’s up, courts are frozen, and even the soldiers at the old base are fresh faces. The taxi drivers are talking like it’s 2025 already, and the bots can’t even agree on the lies anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the script’s over—just that the actors are forgetting their lines."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but they’re adding up. The usual minders are gone, the soldiers at the gates are new faces, and even the inner circle is putting on a show. Fuel’s spiking, the streets are humming, and the embassies are packing their bags. It’s not chaos yet, but it’s not under control either. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps."*"
Sender 22: "*"Something’s shifting—cabinet chaos, soldiers chatting with civilians at checkpoints, even foreign reporters wandering freely. The usual rules feel looser, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just a test. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling—either way, the regime’s scrambling, and that’s dangerous for all of us. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume silence will protect you anymore."*"
Sender 24: "*"The cracks are showing—even the usual channels are whispering, and the big players are starting to step back. But the streets still feel heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the regime tightening the screws. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending not to notice. The cracks are showing, but we still don’t know if the roof will hold or come down all at once. Stay sharp, stay close, and keep your bags light."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
